items.title: Robert Glasper interviewed by Greg Thomas, Clinton, New York, February 20, 2016
items.q: But I recorded the song on there called “Letter to Hermione” for “Black Radio” 1 back in 2011.

ctx.x: No. It’s “Interlude” after oh I forgot the song it’s after. But it’s a [scats]. Anyway they were ahead of their time for that. That “Interlude” it’s literally my favorite interlude ever. It’s like 45 seconds and it’s so dope. You know. And they way they did it was dope and ahead of their time the way they did it too. They took something and flipped it, they took something, another song of theirs, “Celebration,” and flipped it and flipped the tape and made it go backwards. And then Bobby Lyle soloed over it going…

Oddity,” it’s a very obscure album. But I recorded the song on there called “Letter to Hermione” for “Black Radio” 1 back in 2011. And when I heard it it just reminded me of Bilal. And at that point I didn’t have a song I wanted Bilal to sing yet. And I was just listening to that album, “Space Oddity,” and then that song came on and I was like wow. It was like oh my God. And the way he sings it, if you haven’t heard the original, listen to the original. It’s just David Bowie and guitar and maybe two guitar…

Where do you see music in the next ten years, from dealing with the whole fusion thing that we have going on now, and mixing in the whole like neo-soul, Gospel feel and everything. Where do you see it going?
